title: Normalized field-action and point-adjunction data
statement: For a field $k$, a separable closure $k^s/k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology, and a commutative condensed ring $R$, define $\mathrm{FieldData}_R$ to consist of the normalized geometric section data at $s$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent] together with the assertion that its additive functor $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ is an equivalence. Here $\mathcal A_G(R)$ is the internal action category of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. In the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention], use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the actual point and scheme pullback/direct-image functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. An adjunction square consists of comparison isomorphisms for the left and right adjoints whose Hom transposes agree on every morphism; its equation fixes both units and counits. A normalized derived comparison is one satisfying the total-right-derived-unit equation for its specified ordinary comparison. The auxiliary point-adjunction datum uses the actual point module pullback and direct image, requires their additive/exact-inverse-image structures, and fixes unit and counit on underlying abelian sheaves. Scalar extensions and adjunctions are the actual ordinary and total-left-derived constructions of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Forgetting data require exactness and conservativity of the existing action-forgetting functor, also after deriving. These are data types and predicates, with no assertion here that they are inhabited. The auxiliary OrdinaryScalarTransport datum packages exact scalar-action restriction, its additive ordinary left adjoint, the two Hom-normalized scalar adjunction squares, and the identity-on-geometric-sections field comparison with its normalized derived restriction. The canonical shift on derived scalar extension is the left-adjoint shift induced by exact scalar restriction.
